### Interactive tool for model evaluation

::: panel-tabset
## Aim

Our goal is to develop a methodological framework and an interactive tool to evaluate Species Distribution Models (SDMs\*).

To this aim, the **Model Evaluation Tool (MET)** will leverage and integrate the expertise of multiple modelers, developers, taxonomic and survey experts, and managers with the purpose of improving model performance and predictions, extracting strategic information and informing decision making.

What are the problems we're trying to solve?

-   Unfair, ambiguity and disperse critique of modeling

-   Frustrations and miscommunications on both model users and developers

-   Miscommunications with downstream information/opinion-receivers

-   Missed opportunities for model improvements

-   Loss of model information that could be well used for inputs to actions/decisions due to interactions with model outputs that are due to:

    -   Inexplicit modelers and evaluators' purpose(s)

    -   Undisciplined path of model interaction and evaluation

    -   Purposes not well aligned with modeling utility

    -   Model appropriateness regarded as Yes/No instead of gradient of appropriateness

*\* SDMs are numerical tools that combine species occurrences (e.g., presence, presence/absence and counts) with covariates (environmental data sets related to species) to make spatially explicit predictions of habitat suitability or species density, using a variety of algorithms.*

## Approach

#### Integrating multiple interactions, needs and purposes

We proposed that the Model Evaluation Tool (MET) integrates multiple interactions, needs and expectations of modelers and evaluators.

For instance modelers provide not only the outputs of the model (e.g., predictions, uncertainty, etc) but a thorough summary of the model design. See [template here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1BfGmC8uopgqpNw8p-3Pp3IOky_eT_y8kN3-XRCi5jj4/edit?tab=t.0) that modelers will use to populate with their model information, including the main purpose of the model and all technical information used for model development. Modelers usually expect some feedback from evaluators on how to improve model predictions and reduce uncertainty.

However, model evaluators interact with models' outputs, inputs and metadata in at least two non-exclusive ways: providing feedback to the model and extracting information from the model. These interactions are driven by multiple purposes.

For instance, evaluators might provide feedback on some aspects of the model developed by modelers (e.g., some areas seems to be over predicted) and potentially identified the reasons (e.g., observations used might have strong bias because X,Y, Z). Then, modelers implement adjustments based on such feedback, wich can lead to model improvements in performance, spatial predictions, and potentially reduce spatial uncertainty.

However, evaluators might also approach models to extract strategic information they can use for their own purposes. For instance, taxonomic experts would like to know where the species is most likely to be found based on model predictions (if they consider predictions are 'good'), then visit those places (that they have not visited yet) to confirm species presence.

The figure below shows a conceptual framework we used to develop the MET.

![](Figures/Users.jpg)

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Modelers

Modelers are usually quantitative/spatial analysts/coders experts that co-design, implement, test Species Distribution Models (SDMs). They deliver spatially explicit predictions and their associated uncertainty of multiple species within a geographic area of interest. The predictions of SDMs are usually aimed to identify species potential distribution, habitat suitability, relative density, among others
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Evaluators

Evaluators come from multiple disciplines and expertises. For instance, evaluators ca be *taxonomic (e.g., birds) and survey experts* that possess a deep knowledge and understanding of the ecology, biology and the geographic/environmental context of the species. Their knowledge allows them to review part of and/or the entire model, providing feedback to modelers.

Evlauators can also review specific parts of the model. For instance, *statisticians* can review how modelers treated data sets (e.g., aggregating observations) and also assess the appropriateness of statistical analysis and the rigor in meeting statistical assumptions. Other modelers, unrelated to the model's design, can play a significant role in providing feedback on specific aspects of the models (e.g., alternative algorithms, model tuning, etc.).

*Resource managers* can evaluate information needs for multiple applications (e.g., forest management, habitat conservation, co-benefits) when confronting model outputs. They also can assess the risk of implementing a specific scenario due to a certain level of uncertainty.
:::

## Scope

**Presentation**

The ideal Model Evaluation Tool (MET) will have multiple modules to support an adaptive modeling framework and a decision making process. Some of the modules will be functional in the first phase (2025-2026) and others will be developed in a second phase (see figure description below). The core of the MET in this first stage are the Model evaluation and synthesis modules, supported by the model development modules to capture data inputs, outputs and metadata. All of these modules will be integrated in the interactive module to facilitate multiple users navigating, inquiring and reacting to the model in evaluation.

![](Figures/MET_Modules.jpg){fig-align="center"}

**Case studies**

We will evaluate SDMs for multiple species from:

-   The [Ontario Breeding Bird Atlas models (Atlas-3)](https://www.birdsontario.org/).

However, we will be also testing:

-   The upcoming version 5 (V5) models from the [Boreal Avian Modelling project (BAM)](https://borealbirds.ca/new-canada-wide-land-bird-density-estimates-version-4-0/)

**Model development**

The model development section provides assistance to multiple users in designing their model and creating the metadata file (i.e., information about the model). In this stage we will provide also the means to managing and/or uploading spatial and tabular data (see [potential list of inputs, outputs and metadata](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1uyOwWWMrQLy3FudaIarap56AtbVy3PzLj395eDxH2WU/edit?tab=t.0) that developers need to create the interactive tool).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Managing metadata

Model design is a fundamental part of the model cycle and it should be done at the beginning of the process. The ideal situation involves the interaction of multiple users (modelers, evaluators and resource managers), discussing and finding common ground on:

-   Model purpose(s), objective(s).
-   Users needs and expectations.

There is also important to identify and describe key technical elements of the model such as:

-   Inputs required (e.g., focal species, type of data, covariates, scale of the analysis)

-   Potential analysis (e.g., data preparation, algorithms to use, etc.)

-   Expected outputs (e.g., predictions, uncertainty)

-   Main assumptions

This is what we might call model co-design, and we will provide guidance and forms to document and summarize this stage.

However, model co-design is not always possible, so summarizing decisions taken in the designing stage is critical to inform further stages (e.g., model evaluation). [The metadata file](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1BfGmC8uopgqpNw8p-3Pp3IOky_eT_y8kN3-XRCi5jj4/edit?tab=t.0) will provide guidance on how to summarize all elements from the model cycle.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

**Model evaluation**

The modules provide users with an interactive environment to provide feedback on model inputs, outputs and metadata, and extract strategic information (see a[list of potential purposes from the model evaluator perspective](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1X9aWBEglsdX3KFxEnwaNq414oljZK11UXlov_jxGPtY/edit?gid=0#gid=0) that will drive the extraction of information from the model).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Model evaluation

-   Review information and provide feedback.

-   Store, analyze, summarize and make recommendations

![](Figures/Model_Evaluation.jpg)
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Model synthesis

It will allow elevators to compare their overall ranking evaluation with model performance metrics.

It will also allow evaluators to retrieve the summary of their evaluation, including all feedback provided and a summary of the strategic information.

In future developments, AI will be incorporated to compile and analyze evaluators steps taken in the model evaluation process.
:::

**Model application**

Evaluating and interpreting the effect of model uncertainty for multiple decisions and applications.
